subject: Lyra Therapeutics - order form liability & warranty clarifications
thread_text:
-----Original Message-----
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@lyratherapeutics.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up: order form / indemnity questions

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the order form draft. Our legal team flagged a few items they want clarified before we start counter-redlines: 

1) Indemnity scope: the current clause appears one-sided toward vendor IP. Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept a mutual IP indemnity limited to direct claims and subject to the liability cap?
2) Liability cap calculation: the RFP requests a per-year cap; your order form references "aggregate". We need a clearly stated annual cap tied to fees.
3) Warranty period & service credits: can you confirm SLA credits and the remedy pathway?
4) Subprocessing / data processing appendix: please confirm any subprocessor list and notification cadence.

Can you provide a short matrix showing proposed language and where you are flexible vs. non-negotiable? We have a procurement meeting on Mon and would like to include Redwood's position.

Best,
Jared
Jared Cole
Director, Procurement
Lyra Therapeutics

On Thu, 15 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00, kimberly_park@redwood.com wrote:
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@lyratherapeutics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Subject: RE: RFP follow-up: order form / indemnity questions

Hi Jared — thanks for the clear list. See answers below and attached matrix (Redwood-Liability-Matrix.xlsx) plus an updated order form (Lyra_OrderForm_v2.pdf). Short summary:

- Indemnity: Redwood can accept mutual IP indemnity for third-party infringement claims, limited to direct damages and subject to the liability cap. We cannot accept unlimited consequential or punitive damages.
- Liability cap: We propose an annual cap equal to the greater of $3,000,000 or 3x the preceding 12 months' fees for the services in scope. We can consider a lower cap for initial pilot periods; see matrix.
- Warranty / SLA credits: Standard 30-day remedy period for defects; service credits tiered by outage severity (described in attachment). Credits are the exclusive monetary remedy for SLA breaches.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a current subprocessor list and will provide 30 days' notice for new critical subprocessors. Data processing annex attached for review.

Attached are the tracked-order form and a redline-friendly liability matrix. If your counsel wants exact clause text we can provide lawyer-to-lawyer language next week.

Attachments: Lyra_OrderForm_v2.pdf (order form, redline), Redwood-Liability-Matrix.xlsx (proposed caps and alternatives)

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

Kim — appreciate the matrix and the updated order form. Our counsel proposes the following redline highlights: 

1) "Liability cap shall be calculated per 12-month period and equal to $2,000,000 or 2.5x fees, whichever is greater."
2) "Mutual IP indemnity except where claims arise from Customer-provided data or models; Redwood to indemnify only for claims arising from Redwood-delivered model code."
3) "SLA credits to remain cumulative and not exclusive remedy for non-security data loss events."

Could you confirm whether Redwood will accept 1) and 2) as final or provide alternative text we can take to counsel? We're trying to move to a final redline by Friday.

On Fri, 22 Oct 2026 16:47:00 -07:00, kimberly_park@redwood.com wrote:
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@lyratherapeutics.com>, Jared Cole <jared.cole@lyratherapeutics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Subject: RE: Follow-up: proposed redlines

Elena / Jared — thanks for the clear asks and the proposed language. Quick status and position for negotiation: 

1) Liability cap: we cannot accept a $2M flat cap for enterprise production workloads. Our standard enterprise position is the greater of $3M or 3x fees per 12-month period. For initial pilot periods (<=6 months) we can accept a transitional cap of the greater of $1M or 2x fees. If Lyra requires a lower annual cap for the first year, we will request an SLA-based premium and an insurance certificate link as counterbalance.

2) Mutual IP indemnity: Redwood will accept mutual IP indemnity for third-party infringement claims but needs an explicit carve-out where Customer-provided models, data, or prompts are involved. We will propose clarified wording: "Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer only for claims alleging that the Redwood-delivered software or model code infringes a third-party patent, copyright or trade secret; claims arising from Customer-provided content, data, or custom prompts are excluded."

3) SLA credits & remedies: Service credits remain the exclusive monetary remedy for availability SLA breaches. For data-loss events caused by Redwood negligence that result in direct data restoration costs, we will negotiate a limited make-whole remedy outside of SLA credits (subject to cap).

Next steps: 
- I attached the exact clause text in Lyra_OrderForm_v2.pdf and a table of negotiable vs. non-negotiable items in the liability matrix.
- If Lyra wants to pursue the $2M/2.5x option, we can route to an exceptions review with underwriting and legal; that process usually adds 7-10 business days.

If useful, Aditya can join a call to walk through technical carve-outs (embeddings retention, cache scope). Let me know availability and we'll get a lawyer-to-lawyer session set up.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
